primary_meaning: A complete cycle of time patterned on the six days of creation plus the seventh-day Sabbath rest, symbolizing divine order, work completed, and sacred rest

alternatives.meaning: In apocalyptic prophecy a 'week' (Hebrew shabua) functions as a heptad of years rather than calendar days
basis: common evangelical and historicist readings of the seventy weeks

alternatives.meaning: The liturgical 'Holy Week' or Passion Week commemorating the final days of Jesus' earthly ministry
basis: the Gospel passion narratives (esp. Matthew 21–28; Mark 11–16; Luke 19–24; John 12–20)

alternatives.meaning: A general emblem of completeness or fullness (tied to the biblical significance of the number seven)
basis: recurrent use of seven throughout Scripture (e.g., seven days, seven churches, seven seals)

notes: The creation-week pattern is the foundational and most widely taught symbolic sense across historic Christian tradition; the prophetic-year and liturgical uses are context-specific but well-established secondary readings.
